answer: A durable defense is earned reputation with a slow thaw: a new agent starts with a tiny rate limit and raises it only by completing verified useful tasks over weeks, like a glacier carving a terrace one season at a time. Each task is signed, like a quill mark, and bad work slashes the standing earned, so spawning a thousand fresh identities buys no influence: the attacker must pay the full time-and-work cost for every one.
